title: Velocimeter performance tiles: compact per-model & per-route UX and chart specs
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: Design a compact set of 'Velocimeter' performance tiles to sit inside Per-Model and Per-Route pages in Redwood Console. Each tile is a self-contained micro-dashboard showing: a P50/P95 latency summary with trend, throughput sparkline (req/s), token-rate mini-sankey (input vs output tokens), and a cost-per-token microbar. Tiles must be legible at small sizes, keyboard accessible, and function as a quick-launch to the full performance canvas. This ticket contains UX flows, micro-interaction specs, and explicit chart rendering rules for frontend engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Velocimeter tile implemented as a responsive component at 280x120 and 420x160 sizes
Latency view shows P50, P95 numeric + delta vs 24h baseline and a 7-day sparkline
Throughput sparkline supports 60s, 5m, 1h zooms via hover scrub
Token sankey simplified to two bars showing avg input and avg output tokens, with percent change badge
Cost-per-token microbar uses color banding with clear thresholds: <=$0.002 (green), $0.002-$0.01 (amber), >$0.01 (red)
Tile passes keyboard navigation and screen reader label checks (WCAG AA recommended), including label text for each metric
Prototype links and component contract reviewed by Eng and PM and merged into story branch
Performance metrics default to 95th percentile aggregation for latency for model routes with >1000 req/day, otherwise show p50 + sample count
design_notes: Tile is intended for rapid triage: emphasize delta% and color-coded risk over raw numbers
Primary interaction is click -> expands to full route performance panel with traces and token waterfall
When a route has a live rollout in progress, tile includes a 10px banner at top with rollout state (canary/AB/rollback) and an action 'Open Rollout'
Use subtle micro-animations for sparkline load and delta badge transitions to signal freshness; animations must be no longer than 160ms and prefer transform/opacity only
Avoid heavy legends: inline labels only; hover reveals exact time-series tooltip
For highly skewed latency distributions, tile should present a mini-violin overlay behind the sparkline at larger size (420x160 only)
Default timezone and aggregation window respects console settings; tile can be pinned to a custom timezone via right-click menu
chart_specs: Latency metric (numbers): font-family Inter, weight 600 at 16px for primary value, 12px for P95 label
Latency delta: small capsule with background-color #F1F8F6 for positive (improved), #FFF5F0 for negative (regressed); arrows use system icons
Sparkline (throughput): single-line area with 1px stroke #2B8AF6 and 20% opacity fill #2B8AF6 0.2; stroke cap round; sampling bucket 10s for 60s view, 1m for 5m, 5m for 1h
Sparkline hover tooltip: shows timestamp ISO8601, req/s to 2 decimals, 95th latency at that point

Token mini-sankey: represented as two horizontally stacked bars, left=avg input tokens, right=avg output tokens; bar color input #7C3AED, output #06B6D4; center line shows token-preservation ratio as percent

Cost microbar: horizontal scale with three bands colored green (#10B981), amber (#F59E0B), red (#EF4444); indicator dot with numeric label left-aligned; hover shows breakdown: model compute, quantization overhead, caching savings
Thresholds: latency warning threshold configurable per model but defaults: P95 > 500ms -> amber band; P95 > 1200ms -> red band
Data freshness indicator: small dot top-right of tile; green for <30s, amber for <5m, gray stale after 10m
Rendering guidance: use canvas-backed rendering for sparklines when >100 tiles are on screen; otherwise SVG is acceptable
Accessibility: all charts must expose a terse aria-label summarizing P50, P95, throughput, and cost with language: 'P50 120ms, P95 430ms, throughput 24 req per second, cost $0.003 per token'.
review_comments: PM (Priya Kapoor): 'Love the compactness. Can we surface a 'sticky pin' affordance to keep a tile pinned to console header? Might be a separate ticket.'
Eng (Liam O'Connor): 'Chart sampling granularities look good. Concern: mini-sankey adds DOM complexity; propose canvas fallback and precomputed aggregates from metrics pipeline.'
SRE (Natalie Chen): 'Add rate-limit on tile refreshes per user to avoid DDoS on metrics endpoints. 1s min per tile.'
Design Lead (Marianne Li): 'Make sure colorblind-friendly palette available via console settings. Swap purple/turquoise for high-contrast variant.'
Accessibility Reviewer (Omar Aziz): 'Request explicit aria-describedby mapping to detailed panel. Also ensure keyboard focus exposes tooltip data by pressing Space/Enter.'
decisions: Go with canvas rendering for token sankey and sparklines when tile-count > 40 on screen (decision backed by Eng perf spike)
Default latency aggregation will surface P95 for high-volume routes; lower-volume routes show P50 + sample count
Sankey simplified to two-bar model to reduce cognitive overhead; full multi-node flow will remain in full performance canvas
Include rollout banner only when rollout status != stable to avoid visual noise

Engineering: implement Storybook component + canvas fallback (Liam) - estimate 3
Backend: metrics endpoint flag for 'velocimeter-aggregates' to return pre-aggregated buckets (SRE) - estimate 2
PM: coordinate E2E test plan and rollout canary (Priya) - due 2025-11-18
QA: create accessibility test cases (Omar) - due 2025-11-15
notes_for_engineering: Expose an event 'velocimeter.open' with payload {route_id, model_id, time_window} when tile is clicked
Telemetry: emit metric 'ui.velocimeter.render_ms' and sample tile freshness state
Fallback behavior: if any primary metric fails to load, show skeleton and a single-line error link 'Retry' which triggers fetch with exponential backoff
final_notes: Please review chart color tokens and accessibility copy. After sign-off, schedule a week-of canary on staging for core accounts. Aim to ship with console-2025.11 release window.
